profile.reading: Menlo Digital's MD-DC1 facility, part of the operator's MD-VA1 Herndon campus, sits at 13775 McLearen Road, Herndon, Virginia 20171, in Fairfax County's Northern Virginia data center market. Per the operator's own project page, the facility was under construction as of the most recent research pass, with Fairfax County approvals secured and construction commencing in the first quarter of 2025. Dominion Energy is delivering 67.2 megawatts of utility power to the site from its Lincoln Park Substation, which was energized in December 2024. The operator's own page states a planned 48 megawatts of critical IT load once complete, a figure recorded here as planned rather than operating capacity given the facility's construction status, and a total of 307,498 square feet. Herndon sits within the broader Northern Virginia Data Center Alley region, immediately adjacent to major hyperscale and colocation clusters in Ashburn and Sterling tracked elsewhere in this registry, drawing developers like Menlo Digital with access to Dominion Energy's high voltage transmission infrastructure and the region's dense fiber connectivity. Menlo Digital is a data center developer building purpose designed facilities for enterprise and hyperscale tenants. No founding date, headquarters address, or company wide portfolio detail was located for the operator itself in available sourcing this session. A PR Newswire release on the groundbreaking describes Menlo Digital as a vertically integrated data center platform under Menlo Equities, a private real estate investment and development firm with more than 25 years developing specialized technology facilities, headquartered in Menlo Park, California, with a national development pipeline exceeding 1.8 gigawatts across five markets: Northern Virginia, Phoenix, Silicon Valley, Dallas, and Chicago. The release describes this Herndon building as a two story, 307,000 square foot structure configured as four 12 megawatt data halls, with 67 megawatts of utility power from Dominion Energy Virginia, a powered shell delivery targeted for summer 2026, and Clune Construction serving as general contractor. Menlo Digital's Chief Development Officer, Jane Vaughan, is quoted in the release describing the groundbreaking as part of a broader national expansion strategy rather than a single, isolated project.

reading.body:
Menlo Digital's MD-DC1 in Herndon, Virginia is under construction with 48 megawatts of planned IT capacity and 67.2 megawatts of utility power already connected as of December 2024.

The facility spans 307,498 square feet across the MD-VA1 campus in Fairfax County. Dominion Energy energized the Lincoln Park Substation connection in late 2024, ahead of the data center's operational timeline. Construction commenced in the first quarter of 2025 following Fairfax County approval.

The 67.2 megawatts of utility power exceeds the planned 48 megawatts of IT capacity, indicating either planned headroom for future expansion, losses in power delivery, or cooling infrastructure. This gap between utility supply and compute capacity is typical in data center design but constrains how much computing load can actually run at this location.

The research underlying this profile is complete as of September 2026. The facility remains under construction and has not yet reported operating capacity.
